Reviewer action: approve the named capability refinement only if the public safety and EOD framing remains bounded.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: replace broad platform language with the actual enzyme pair, perfusion approach, measured antigen-removal result, human-decedent kidney milestone, and the observed antigen-regeneration constraint. Evidence: peer-reviewed Nature Communications and Nature Biomedical Engineering articles describe two Flavonifractor plautii enzymes, approximately 80% A-antigen loss within two hours under normothermic or hypothermic perfusion, and a converted kidney transplanted into a type-O brain-dead recipient without hyperacute rejection; the later study also records antigen regeneration and immune-mediated signs beginning after day two. Mission/Public Need read: Avivo's work addresses blood and organ compatibility while the published Medical Treatment and Evacuation need requires scalable treatment under constrained conditions; this suggests a long-horizon medical-logistics relevance, not current field readiness. Unknowns: regulatory pathway, clinical-trial status, manufacturing scale, shelf life, field workflow, safety, efficacy, NATO DIANA milestones, and defence deployment are not public. Reviewer action: approve only as preclinical translational maturity with the limitations in the summary.
reviewWarnings: The cited transplant was a preclinical human-decedent model, not a completed clinical trial or approved therapy.
Antigen re-expression and later immune-mediated signs are material constraints and must remain visible.
Do not infer field readiness, regulatory approval, manufacturing scale, procurement eligibility, or military adoption.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: turn the sparse XMA-11K entry into an actionable recovery-beacon record with power, life, RF, channel, interface, pressure-test, and physical details, and add current OceanWave development activity to the organization profile. Evidence: the official XMA brochure and manual specify Argos PTT operation, 11,000-metre rating, battery options, more than 96 days at the default interval, 1-watt output, selectable 401.63–401.656 MHz channels, serial programming, and a self-contained submersible form; Xeos's technology page describes 20,000-psi design testing, while NRC records a 2025–2026 OceanWave sensor contribution. Mission/Public Need read: full-ocean-depth asset recovery and current wave-sensor development can support persistent ocean sensing, while the Persistent Uncrewed Underwater Surveillance need requires sustained detection and notification; neither source proves surveillance payload performance or defence integration. Unknowns: Argos service dependencies, surfacing trigger, acoustic release integration, classified use, validation standards, OceanWave specifications, customer use, and current defence contracts are not public. Reviewer action: approve the technical XMA refinement and bounded current-activity note without creating an OceanWave capability yet.
reviewWarnings: The XMA-11K is an asset-recovery beacon, not an underwater surveillance sensor by itself.
The OceanWave award establishes development activity but does not publish a product specification or deployment.
Historical federal contracts are not current demand and are not added as active relationships.
